original_question: Given an arbitrary hyperelliptic cover C -> P^1 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, is it possible to deform C to an ordinary hyperelliptic curve while moving only one branch point?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies that the problem is about an arbitrary hyperelliptic cover over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, asks for deformation to an ordinary hyperelliptic curve, and imposes the key restriction that only one branch point may move. This matches the wording and scope of Question 5.7 almost verbatim.
missing_details: The paper's Section 5 works over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, and from Section 5.3 onward it assumes p > 2; this odd-characteristic restriction is important because the branch-point formulation of hyperelliptic covers is being used.
The cover should be understood as a smooth hyperelliptic cover C -> P^1_k of some fixed genus g.
'Ordinary' should be made explicit: the deformed curve should have p-rank equal to its genus g, equivalently Jac(C)[p] ≅ (Z/p ⊕ mu_p)^g.
'Moving only one branch point' should be unpacked as varying the hyperelliptic cover through hyperelliptic covers while keeping all the other branch points fixed.
The genus is implicit in the draft; the deformation is within the same hyperelliptic genus.

The paper immediately gives an equivalent rephrasing in terms of a fixed branch locus Lambda = {lambda_1,...,lambda_2g} of a genus g-1 hyperelliptic curve and asking for one extra point mu so that the resulting genus g hyperelliptic curve branched at {lambda_1,...,lambda_2g, infinity, mu} is ordinary.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 2, and let C -> P^1_k be a smooth hyperelliptic cover of genus g. Is every such C deformable, through hyperelliptic covers of P^1_k of the same genus, to an ordinary hyperelliptic curve by varying only one of its branch points while keeping all the other branch points fixed?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_2g} is the branch locus of an arbitrary hyperelliptic curve of genus g - 1 over k, does there exist a point mu in A^1_k \ Lambda such that the smooth hyperelliptic curve branched at {lambda_1, ..., lambda_2g, infinity, mu} is ordinary?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 5 of the paper, not the unrelated first section. The exact nearest formulation is Question 5.7: 'Given an arbitrary hyperelliptic cover C -> P^1_k, is it possible to deform C to an ordinary hyperelliptic curve by moving only one of the branch points?' (Section 5.4, Question 5.7, p. 15). Section 5.2 supplies the needed notation: k is algebraically closed of characteristic p, and a genus-g curve is ordinary when its p-rank is g, equivalently when its Jacobian has p-torsion (Z/p ⊕ mu_p)^g (Section 5.2, pp. 12-13). The odd-characteristic hypothesis is inherited from the sentence 'For the rest of the paper, suppose p > 2' in Section 5.3 (p. 13). The paper itself immediately rephrases Question 5.7 in branch-locus language, which gives the only alternate formulation that should be used here (Section 5.4, p. 15). The surrounding context shows the intent is narrow: an affirmative answer would support the authors' expected description of the generic p-torsion on V_{g,g-2} ∩ H_g via their fibre-product construction, so this is not meant as a broader deformation question (Section 5.3, Corollary 5.2 and the discussion leading into Question 5.7, pp. 14-15).
